# Assurly

> A pre-deploy ship gate for AI-built SaaS. Scan a deployed URL or a Next.js + Supabase + Stripe + Vercel codebase and get one verdict — ship or don't — before it reaches production.

Assurly exists for people who build fast with AI tools (Lovable, v0, Bolt, Cursor, Replit) and are not security specialists. Those tools produce working code quickly but routinely leave the production wiring unfinished: a database table without row-level security, a payment webhook that never verifies its signature, a service key that ships to the browser.

It answers one question — "can I ship this right now?" — with a Ship Score out of 100 and one of three verdicts: READY TO SHIP, REVIEW RECOMMENDED, or NOT READY TO SHIP. Findings come with the exact fix (the SQL statement, the config change), not just a warning.

Source code is analysed locally by the CLI and the MCP server and is never uploaded. The hosted product additionally probes a live URL and can open fix pull requests.

Operated by Tibor Kútik, Kolta, Slovakia. The published packages are MIT licensed.

## Packages

- [assurly](https://www.npmjs.com/package/assurly): the CLI. `npx assurly scan` runs the gate locally, exits non-zero when blocked, so it drops into CI.
- [@assurly/mcp-server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@assurly/mcp-server): the same gate over the Model Context Protocol, so an AI agent in Cursor or Claude Code can check its own work before shipping.
- [@assurly/scanner-core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@assurly/scanner-core): the rules on their own, for building other tooling. Runs in Node or the browser.

## What it checks

Thirteen rule areas, all evaluated locally:

- Supabase row-level security gaps and exposed service-role keys
- Stripe webhook signature verification and replay/idempotency protection
- Secrets and undocumented environment variables reaching the client bundle
- React Server Component data leaks
- SQL and migration safety
- Serverless connection pooling
- Vercel edge-runtime compatibility
- Cold-start cost
- TypeScript strictness
- Missing CI checks
- Install-time trust under npm 12 (see below)
- The AI agent's own tooling and MCP configuration (see below)
- Dependency provenance and typo/slop-squatting risk

## Which of my dependencies can run code when I install them?

`npx assurly scan --supply`

npm 12 stopped running install scripts by default, so every project now records which dependencies it trusts to execute code during installation in an `allowScripts` allowlist. A bare package name in that allowlist grants execution to every version of the package, forever — including a version published later by whoever takes the package over. An exact version pin does not.

Assurly reads that allowlist, the lockfile's install-script flags, and non-registry dependencies, entirely offline. npm only reads `allowScripts` from the workspace root, so a declaration in a sub-workspace is silently ignored — Assurly reports that too.

## Can it audit the AI agent's own setup?

`npx assurly scan --agent`

It reads MCP client configuration and agent instruction files and reports MCP servers that run shell commands, remote endpoints on plain `http://`, credentials written into config files, and instructions hidden from human readers but visible to models.

## How do I let an AI agent run the gate itself?

`npx -y @assurly/mcp-server` exposes five tools over MCP: `assurly_scan_path`, `assurly_scan_files`, `assurly_scan_agent`, `assurly_explain_rule` and `assurly_verdict`.

It works with Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code and Windsurf. When the verdict is blocked the tool returns an error rather than a passing result, so the agent stops instead of shipping. `assurly_verdict` reads the hosted API only and never scans locally. Per-client setup: https://assurly.dev/mcp

## How do I run it in CI?

`npx assurly scan` exits non-zero when the verdict is blocked, so it works as an ordinary CI step with no plugin. `assurly init` writes a GitHub Actions workflow. Local scans need no API key and no account.

## Pricing

- Free — unlimited local CLI scans, the live URL proof-probe, one guarded app, MCP server access.
- Pro, $19 per month (€17) — unlimited guarded apps, continuous monitoring on every deploy, AI deep review, auto-fix pull requests, private repository scanning.
- OEM / Platform — usage- and seat-based, quoted directly. Keyed verdict API for your own users and higher rate limits.

## What Assurly does not claim

It is not SOC 2 audited and does not hold ISO/IEC 27001 certification, and says so on its own trust page. It carries no customer testimonials, because it has no customers yet.
